title: Free-orbit criterion for simplicial module cell filtrations
statement:
Use simplicial sets, simplicial subsets, faces and degenerate simplices from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and the simplicial monoid/action conventions of [def-coef-coherent-monad-modules]. Let $M$ be a simplicial monoid, $X$ a left simplicial $M$-module, and $A$ an $M$-submodule of $X$. For a simplicial set $K$, the free module $M\times K$ has $M$ acting on the first factor. Suppose given an ordinal $\lambda$ and $M$-submodules $X_\alpha\subseteq X$, $\alpha\leq\lambda$, increasing in $\alpha$, with $X_0=A$, $X_\lambda=X$, and $X_\beta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\beta}X_\alpha$ for every limit $\beta\leq\lambda$. For every $\alpha<\lambda$ suppose given a set $R_\alpha$ of simplices $\sigma\in (X_{\alpha+1})_{n_\sigma}$ such that every proper face of every $\sigma\in R_\alpha$ lies in $X_\alpha$, and such that for every $k\geq0$ the map
$$\coprod_{\sigma\in R_\alpha}\{(m,\theta): m\in M_k,\ \theta:[k]\to[n_\sigma]\ \text{surjective}\}\longrightarrow (X_{\alpha+1})_k\setminus(X_\alpha)_k,\qquad (m,\theta)\mapsto m\cdot(\theta^*\sigma),$$
is well defined (each $m\cdot\theta^*\sigma$ lies outside $X_\alpha$) and bijective. Then each square with top $\coprod_{\sigma\in R_\alpha}M\times\partial\Delta^{n_\sigma}\to X_\alpha$ (induced by the faces of the $\sigma$) and bottom $\coprod_{\sigma\in R_\alpha}M\times\Delta^{n_\sigma}\to X_{\alpha+1}$, $(m,\tau)\mapsto m\cdot\tau^*\sigma$, is a pushout of left simplicial $M$-modules. Hence $A\to X$ is a small relative projective cell complex in left simplicial $M$-modules: a transfinite composite, continuous at limit ordinals, of pushouts of coproducts of free-module maps $M\times\partial\Delta^n\to M\times\Delta^n$, $n\geq0$. If $A$ is empty, $X$ is a cellular weight for the one-object simplicial category with endomorphism monoid $M$, meaning that $\varnothing\to X$ is such a cell complex.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3 (relative projective cells), together with the skeletal cell argument used in Lemma 6.1.8. Read online; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha<\lambda$ and form the object $P_\alpha$ by the displayed pushout: in simplicial degree $k$ it is the quotient of $(X_\alpha)_k\amalg\coprod_{\sigma\in R_\alpha}(M_k\times(\Delta^{n_\sigma})_k)$ which identifies $(m,\tau)$ whenever $\tau$ factors through a proper face of $[n_\sigma]$, with that element identified with $m\cdot\tau^*\sigma$ in $(X_\alpha)_k$. The relation is preserved by every simplicial operator and by the $M$-action, because the boundary inclusions and the maps induced by the faces of $\sigma$ are simplicial and equivariant. Thus $P_\alpha$ is a left simplicial $M$-module and the bottom map induces an equivariant simplicial map $\phi_\alpha:P_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3, construction of the relative cell pushout

proof.text: The map $\phi_\alpha$ is surjective in degree $k$. An element of $(X_\alpha)_k$ is already represented by the old summand. For an element outside $(X_\alpha)_k$, the assumed bijection supplies a unique $\sigma\in R_\alpha$, $m\in M_k$, and a surjection $\theta:[k]\to[n_\sigma]$ with the element equal to $m\cdot\theta^*\sigma$; it is represented by $(m,\theta)$ in the cell summand. If a cell simplex is indexed by a non-surjective $\tau:[k]\to[n_\sigma]$, its image lies in a proper face of $\sigma$, hence in $X_\alpha$ by the hypothesis on proper faces, and therefore is represented by the old summand.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.8 skeletal cell argument and Proposition 5.3.3

proof.text: The map $\phi_\alpha$ is injective in degree $k$. A representative from the old summand cannot have the same image as a representative $(m,\theta)$ with $\theta$ surjective, since the former lies in $X_\alpha$ and the latter lies outside it. Two surjective representatives have equal images only when their triples $(\sigma,m,\theta)$ agree, by the assumed degreewise bijection. Every non-surjective representative is identified in the quotient with its image in the old summand; if two such representatives have the same image, they become equal through that common old element. Hence the quotient has exactly one representative for every element of $(X_{\alpha+1})_k$, and $\phi_\alpha$ is bijective.

The preceding degreewise bijection is compatible with all simplicial operators and with the $M$-action by construction, so $\phi_\alpha$ is an isomorphism of left simplicial $M$-modules. Equivalently, the square in the statement is a pushout: for any left simplicial $M$-module $Y$, a map from $P_\alpha$ to $Y$ is exactly a map $X_\alpha\to Y$ together with equivariant maps from each $M\times\Delta^{n_\sigma}$ to $Y$ whose restrictions to $M\times\partial\Delta^{n_\sigma}$ agree with the prescribed face maps. This is the universal property of the displayed pushout, checked degreewise on the quotient.

At every successor ordinal the inclusion $X_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}$ is therefore a pushout of a coproduct of free-module maps $M\times\partial\Delta^{n_\sigma}\to M\times\Delta^{n_\sigma}$. At a limit ordinal the given equality $X_\beta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\beta}X_\alpha$ is precisely continuity of the composite. Consequently $A=X_0\to X=X_\lambda$ is a transfinite composite, continuous at limits, of such pushouts; the indexing sets are small sets in the ambient universe, so this is a small relative projective cell complex. When $A=\varnothing$, the same construction is the stated cellular weight for the one-object simplicial category with endomorphism monoid $M$.

The quotient pushout is analyzed in each simplicial degree; non-surjective operators land in old faces, while the assumed orbit bijection gives unique representatives for new simplices. Equivariance, the pushout universal property, and transfinite continuity then give the relative projective cell complex and the empty-base cellular-weight clause. No new nodes were necessary.
